description:
Learn how to edit and mix your tracks to perfection in Suno Studio 2.0. Join Adam McFarland as he explores advanced stem separation, removing baked-in effects, and using clip fades and automation to polish your song.

Watch the full Studio 2.0 series here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLcGl48v5p95s

Timestamps:
0:00 - Introduction to editing and mixing
0:50 - Stem separation and advanced split
1:53 - Auditioning your separated stems
3:16 - Deep dive into mixing with compression and EQ
4:33 - Adding reverb to specific instruments
5:28 - Removing baked-in effects from generated audio
7:38 - Applying clip fades to smooth transitions
8:09 - Using automation on effect parameters
8:52 - Outro

Hosted by Adam McFarland

#SunoStudio #SunoV2 #MusicProduction #AudioMixing #AI

comments.text:
I think all the new features Suno keeps adding are great. But as a producer, there is something even more important to me: *Suno should reliably recognize when I am the creator and rights holder of a song.*

I have already experienced a situation where I wanted to continue working on a song that I had created myself and/or developed in Suno using my own uploaded material. Suno apparently recognized the song – but then prevented me from working with it because the song was already known or published and asked me to prove that I owned the rights.

This is exactly where the recognition system should become smarter: If Suno recognizes a song, it should also be able to recognize *where it knows that song from and that the same user who originally created or uploaded it is now trying to continue working on it.*

As the creator, I should always be able to continue developing my own song – for example, creating versions in other languages, acoustic or unplugged versions, a cappella versions, alternative arrangements, or other variations. I should not suddenly be locked out of my own song simply because Suno already recognizes it.

New production, mixing, and effects features are absolutely welcome. But for me, *reliable creator/ownership recognition and the ability to continue working on my own music at any time* would be an even more important improvement.
